title: Heatwave conditions in eight TN districts; rain likely in Western Ghats - Social News XYZ
full_text:
Chennai, July 27 (SocialNews.XYZ) The Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC), Chennai, has forecast a rise in daytime temperatures across parts of Tamil Nadu over the next few days, with maximum temperatures expected to remain significantly above normal in eight interior districts until July 30.
At the same time, the weather department has predicted light to moderate rainfall in the Western Ghats and parts of the northern coastal region, offering some relief in isolated areas.
According to the latest weather bulletin, maximum temperatures in Vellore, Erode, Karur, Dindigul, Madurai, Virudhunagar, Thoothukudi and Tirunelveli districts are likely to be 2 degrees to 4 degrees Celsius above normal at a few places.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has advised residents in these districts to take adequate precautions against prolonged exposure to heat, particularly during the afternoon hours when temperatures are expected to peak.
The forecast comes at a time when several parts of Tamil Nadu are witnessing warm and humid weather despite intermittent rainfall in some regions.
Meteorologists said the elevated temperatures are likely to persist through July 30 before showing signs of moderation, depending on evolving weather systems over the Bay of Bengal and surrounding regions.
In contrast to the hot conditions expected across the interior districts, the RMC has predicted light to moderate rainfall over the hilly areas of the Western Ghats until July 30. The rainfall is expected to provide some respite from the prevailing heat and support local agricultural activity in the hill regions.
The weather department has also forecast light to moderate rain at one or two places over North Coastal Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal from Tuesday through July 30.
While widespread rainfall is not anticipated, isolated showers are likely to occur under favourable atmospheric conditions.
For Chennai, the RMC has forecast partly cloudy skies over the coming days. Some parts of the city may experience light rain, particularly during the evening or night, though no heavy rainfall has been predicted.
Daytime conditions are expected to remain warm and humid, with temperatures staying close to seasonal levels. The Meteorological Department has urged the public to remain updated with the latest weather advisories, especially in districts expected to experience above-normal temperatures.
People have also been advised to avoid prolonged exposure to the sun during peak afternoon hours, stay well hydrated and take necessary precautions against heat-related illnesses, while residents in areas likely to receive rain should remain alert to local weather updates.
